news.headline: Dynatrace Weighs Overage Fees as It Seeks to Turn Rising Usage Into Recurring Revenue Growth
news.quote: Dynatrace (NYSE:DT) is considering changes to how it charges customers who exceed their subscription commitments

touches.claim: Annual revenue growth slowed from 23% to 19%, six-month revenue growth slowed to 17%, and the dollar-based net retention rate declined from 111% to 109%.
Customers have no obligation to renew their agreements, and large accounts may demand substantial price concessions or elongate strategic deal cycles.

The platform integrates across hybrid, multicloud ecosystems—including AWS, Azure, and GCP—and on-premises systems, using the Dynatrace Platform Subscription (DPS) model to encourage broad capability adoption without overage penalties.

Market maturation, competing offerings, tariffs or tax changes, and large global accounts demanding price concessions create pricing pressure, while customers have no obligation to renew contracts on existing terms.
Management uses the Dynatrace Platform Subscription licensing model to drive broader platform consumption, which grew in excess of 20% year-over-year in the second quarter of fiscal 2027.

For existing-customer expansion to continue, customers must renew their agreements, maintain spending levels, successfully integrate Dynatrace into their technologies, and find the DPS pricing model favorable.

news.why: Dynatrace is weighing overage fees for customers exceeding subscription commitments to convert rising usage into recurring revenue, which directly alters the no-overage-penalty DPS pricing model.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 business description
business_model.claim: Dynatrace sells an AI-powered observability platform. It also covers application security and agentic AI operations, aimed at IT operations, development, security, business and executive teams.
quotes: Dynatrace combines broad and deep observability, continuous runtime application security, and advanced agentic AI operations to deliver answers and intelligent automation across IT operations, development, security, business, and executive teams.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 business description
business_model.claim: Customers are mainly large enterprises: about 4,100 customers in over 110 countries, with the direct sales team targeting the largest 15,000 companies globally.
quotes: As of March 31, 2026, we had approximately 4,100 customers in over 110 countries.
Dynatrace addresses customer needs at various scales and sizes, but our global direct sales team targets the largest 15,000 companies globally.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A and the 10-Q income statement
business_model.claim: Revenue is mostly subscription (SaaS, term licenses, maintenance and support), with a small service line for deployment and training. In the quarter ended September 30, 2026, subscription revenue was 553,112 and service revenue 26,806, out of total revenue of 579,918 (table in thousands).
quotes: We generate revenue primarily by selling subscriptions, which we define as SaaS agreements, term-based licenses, and maintenance and support agreements.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 and MD&A
business_model.claim: Customers are mainly licensed under the Dynatrace Platform Subscription (DPS). The customer commits a minimum annual spend at platform level and draws it down by actual usage at a rate card, so revenue depends on consumption as well as the commitment.
quotes: Under the DPS licensing model, a customer makes a minimum annual spend commitment at the platform level and then consumes that commitment based on actual usage and a straightforward rate card.

business_model.claim: Subscription revenue growth in the latest fiscal year came mainly from existing customers expanding use of the platform, plus new customers. Subscription revenue rose $307.6 million, or 19%.
quotes: Subscription revenue increased by $307.6 million, or 19%, in fiscal 2026 compared to fiscal 2025, primarily due to existing customers expanding their use of the Dynatrace platform combined with the adoption of our solutions by new customers.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-Q key metrics table
business_model.claim: Management tracks annual recurring revenue (ARR) and dollar-based net retention. ARR was 2,207,223 (table in thousands), up 16% from 1,899,402. Net retention was 109% against 111% a year earlier.
quotes: We define ARR as the daily revenue of all subscription agreements that are actively generating revenue as of the last day of the reporting period multiplied by 365.

business_model.claim: Revenue growth slowed. Revenue for the six months ended September 30, 2026 grew 17%, against 19% for the prior fiscal year.
quotes: Our revenue for the six months ended September 30, 2026 grew 17% compared to the prior-year period.

business_model.basis: stated in the earnings release; the underlying consumption data is not in the packet
business_model.claim: Management reports that consumption on the platform is growing faster than revenue. Platform consumption grew in excess of 20% year-over-year, with AI customer cohorts consuming more than twice the rate of other customers.
quotes: Platform consumption continued to grow in excess of 20% year-over-year, with AI customer cohorts consuming more than twice the rate of other customers.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 and risk factors
business_model.claim: Sales go through a direct sales team and partners (global system integrators, cloud providers, resellers, technology alliance partners). One channel partner accounted for 10% of revenue in each of the last two fiscal years.
quotes: We take Dynatrace to market through a combination of our global direct sales team and a network of partners, including GSIs, cloud providers, resellers, and technology alliance partners.
For the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, one channel partner accounted for 10% of revenue.

business_model.claim: Billing is mostly annual in advance, so the balance sheet carries large deferred revenue. Current deferred revenue was 1,036,224 against 1,241,488 at March 31, 2026 (table in thousands). Six-month operating cash flow was 347,325, helped by receivable collections.
quotes: We typically invoice SaaS subscription fees and term licenses annually in advance and recognize subscription revenue ratably over the term of the applicable agreement, provided that all other revenue recognition criteria have been satisfied.

business_model.claim: Subscription gross margin was 85% against 86% a year earlier, because cloud hosting costs rose with customer usage. Cost of revenue therefore scales with consumption of the SaaS platform.
quotes: The decrease in gross margin was primarily due to higher cloud-based hosting costs, which were driven by increased customer utilization of the Dynatrace SaaS platform and expanding adoption of platform features.

business_model.claim: Operating costs are mostly people costs. In the latest quarter, research and development was 132,212, sales and marketing 180,269 and general and administrative 58,744 (table in thousands). Sales and marketing was the largest of the three.
quotes: Personnel costs, which consist of salaries, benefits, bonuses, share-based compensation and, with regard to sales and marketing expenses, sales commissions, are the most significant component of our operating expenses.

quotes: We define non-GAAP income from operations as GAAP income from operations adjusted for the following items: share-based compensation; employer payroll taxes on employee stock transactions; amortization of intangibles; and acquisition-related, restructuring, and other non-recurring or unusual items that may arise from time to time.

This guidance reflects the expected contribution from the Arize acquisition, including approximately 200 basis points of ARR growth accretion and 175 basis points of dilution to non-GAAP operating margin for fiscal 2027.
